extracted.intended_audience: readers seeking guidance on polite social behaviour and manners (gentlemen/gentlewomen in company)
extracted.subtask_description: A numbered collection of rules of civility and social etiquette describing appropriate behaviour in walking, conversation, dining, and company — aimed at guiding individuals how to behave courteously in social settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 53d. Run not in the Streets, neither go too slowly nor with Mouth open
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not run in the streets; avoid overly slow walking, having your mouth open, shaking your arms, stamping, shuffling, pulling up stockings in public, walking on the toes, dancing/skip-like steps, striking heels together, or stooping without cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against hurried or precipitate steps and gaping; do not move or stoop the body unduly or let hands hang; avoid striking the ground hard or throwing the feet about; do not display improper gestures (e.g., pulling up stockings in public); remain upright and composed, and do not leave church bareheaded unless devotion requires it.

rubrics_metrics.name: 54th. Play not the Peacock, looking everywhere about you, to See if you be well Deck't
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid strutting or inspecting yourself ostentatiously in public (checking clothes, shoes, stockings), or other vain gestures like carrying a pen in your mouth or behind your ear, putting flowers in ears/hat, or displaying your handkerchief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not leave your room with a pen in mouth or ear; avoid decorative affectations; keep your pocket-handkerchief out of sight but accessible; never offer a handkerchief to someone unless it is clean and hardly unfolded.

rubrics_metrics.name: 55th. Eat not in the Streets, nor in ye House, out of Season
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not eat while walking in the streets, especially in crowds; refrain from eating in the house outside of meal-times, particularly in others' presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid public eating whether alone or with company; if in a house, abstain from snacking out of time when others are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: 56th. Associate yourself with Men of good Quality if you Esteem your own Reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep company with well-bred people; if you cannot find such company, it is better to go alone than to be in bad company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferring virtuous, respectable associates preserves reputation; solitary attendance is preferable to association with ill repute.

rubrics_metrics.name: 57th. In walking up and Down in a House, only with One in Company if he be Greater than yourself, at the first give him the Right hand
rubrics_metrics.description: When walking in a house with someone of superior rank, give them the right hand at the first step, do not stop before they do, do not be the first to turn, and when turning face them; walk slightly behind a person of high rank so as not to inconvenience them but close enough for conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If equal in rank, keep step side-by-side; do not make frequent pauses without reason; those around a central person should turn with him at the same time to show deference.

rubrics_metrics.name: 58th. let your conversation be without malice or envy
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep conversation free from malice and envy; in all cases of passion let reason govern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A tractable, commendable nature is shown by harmless conversation and reasoned control of passions to preserve reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 59th. Never express anything unbecoming, nor Act against the Rules Moral before your inferiours
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not express unbecoming things or act immorally in front of those beneath you in station, since your example can multiply wrongs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid diverting yourself with your inferiors' knowledge of your faults or failures; set a proper example by behaving morally before subordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: 60th. Be not immodest in urging your Friends to Discover a Secret
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not immodestly press a friend to reveal a secret, as accidental disclosure could harm the friendship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect confidences; do not coerce revelations even playfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: 61st. Utter not base and frivilous things amongst grave and Learn'd Men nor very Difficult Questions or Subjects, among the Ignorant
rubrics_metrics.description: When speaking with learned people avoid trifles; when among the ignorant avoid advancing topics they cannot understand; do not always begin with proverbs; avoid out-of-place or shocking subjects and distressing news at banquets or festivities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor conversation to audience; if unpleasant topics arise, skillfully divert; tell dreams only to confidants for interpretation but do not give them belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: 62d. Speak not of doleful Things in a Time of Mirth or at the Table
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid discussing sorrowful, melancholy topics (death, wounds) during times of mirth or at the table; if others mention them, change the discourse when possible; tell dreams only to intimate friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain appropriate tone for the occasion; preserve conviviality at banquets and celebrations by avoiding distressing subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: 63d. A Man ought not to value himself of his Atchievements or rare Qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not parade your achievements, wit, virtue, birth, wealth, or dignities; avoid speaking of high birth or nobility unless obliged, but do not efface yourself entirely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display modesty rather than boasting; appropriate self-restraint in mentioning personal distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: 64th. Break not a Jest where none take pleasure in mirth
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid jesting when it is out of season; do not burst into excessive laughter without reasonable cause and do not laugh at others' misfortunes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect decorum; restraint in laughter and avoidance of deriding misfortune are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 65th. Speak not injurious Words neither in Jest nor Earnest
rubrics_metrics.description: Never give nicknames or mock anyone, whether jokingly or seriously; do not wound others, especially those of distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain respect; avoid scoffing or picquing others in any manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: 66th. Be not forward but friendly and Courteous; the first to Salute hear and answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Be affable and prompt to render kind offices; always be the first to salute, listen carefully and respond; do not withdraw when duty calls you into conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid morose or forbidding deportment; cultivate approachable courtesy and responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: 67th. Detract not from others neither be excessive in Commending
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not speak ill of anyone or gossip about others' affairs; show moderation in your praises and avoid both flattery and sourness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance between undue adulation and harshness; preserve discretion in commentary about others.

rubrics_metrics.name: 68th. Go not thither, where you know not, whether you Shall be Welcome or not. Give not Advice whth being Ask'd & when desired do it briefly
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not force yourself into conversations or consultations where you are not sure of being welcome; never give unsolicited advice unless you have authority; when asked, be brief and reach the point quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect boundaries of company and limit unsolicited interference; brevity and focus when consulted are virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: 69th. If two contend together take not the part of either unconstrained
rubrics_metrics.description: If two people have something to decide do not take either side unless some pressing reason obliges you; avoid obstinacy; in matters of opinion take the more supported side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not thrust yourself as moderator until required; defer to majority or stronger-supported opinion in indifferent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 70th. Reprehend not the imperfections of others for that belongs to Parents Masters and Superiors
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not act as censor or judge of others' faults; that belongs to those with authority; you may show aversion or give advantageous advice sometimes to the guilty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid taking on a moral censor role; reserve correction to proper authorities while showing appropriate disapproval when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: 71st. Gaze not at the marks or blemishes of Others and ask not how they came
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not take pleasure in scrutinising others' defects or blemishes (especially facial), nor inquire about their origin; keep private remarks made to a friend confidential in company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect others' privacy and avoid prying curiosity; preserve secrets entrusted to you.

rubrics_metrics.name: 72d. Speak not in an unknown Tongue in Company but in your own Language and that as those of Quality do
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use a language you are not thoroughly familiar with in conversation unless absolutely necessary; speak in your native tongue with erudition and elegance, not coarsely like common folk; avoid vulgar terms when discussing serious subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe decorum and modesty in discourse; avoid risky or overly free tales and base expressions in elevated matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 73d. Think before you Speak pronounce not imperfectly nor bring out your Words too hastily but orderly and Distinctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not speak unless prepared and having studied the subject; in ordinary conversation avoid periphrases, subtleties, or figures; avoid confused, abrupt, or hesitating delivery and also avoid speaking so slowly as to bore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare remarks; aim for clarity and appropriate pace — neither hurried and garbled nor painfully slow and repetitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: 74th. When Another Speaks be attentive your Self and disturb not the Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen attentively and do not distract listeners; if someone hesitates do not prompt them unless requested or in private; do not interrupt or reply until the speaker has finished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid helping or suggesting words to a faltering speaker in public; restraint in intervening preserves decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: 75th. In the midst of Discourse ask not what it is about; if you Perceive any Stop because of your arrival, request the speaker to Proceed
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not ask the subject of an ongoing discussion upon arrival; courteously request continuation if it has been paused for your arrival; if someone arrives while you speak, give a brief recapitulation of what has been said, especially if the newcomer is of quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid presumption; show civility by facilitating continuity or summarising for honored arrivals.

rubrics_metrics.name: 76th. While you are talking, Point not with your Finger at him of Whom You Discourse nor Approach too near him
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not point at the person you are speaking about with your finger; do not come too near the person to whom you speak, especially near his face which should be treated with reverence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain physical respect and appropriate personal distance during conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 77th. Treat with men at fit Times about Business & Whisper not in the Company of Others
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a private matter to communicate to one of several people who are conversing, state it in three words and do not whisper in his ear; if secret, draw him aside a little and speak in the language understood by those present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle private business discreetly without disturbing others, or modestly remove the person for secrecy.

rubrics_metrics.name: 78th. Make no Comparisons and if any of the Company be Commended for any brave act of Virtue, commend not another for the Same
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstain from making comparisons between people; if someone is praised for a virtue or action do not praise another for the same as comparisons are odious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid juxtaposing persons in ways that may provoke envy or offense; praise should be reserved and non-comparative.

rubrics_metrics.name: 79th. Be not apt to relate News if you know not the truth thereof. In Discoursing of things you Have heard Name not your Author
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not readily repeat rumours unless you have a guarantor of their truth; in recounting such tales do not name your authority unless you are sure they will appreciate it; preserve secrets confided to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid spreading unverified reports and avoid betraying the trust of those who confide in you.

rubrics_metrics.name: 80th. Be not Tedious in Discourse or in reading unless you find the Company pleased therewith
rubrics_metrics.description: When relating, reading, or arguing, be brief especially if the subject is trivial or listeners show weariness; avoid long-windedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch audience engagement and cut short when appropriate; concision is a courtesy.

rubrics_metrics.name: 81st. Be not Curious to Know the Affairs of Others neither approach to those that Speak in Private
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not show curiosity about others' affairs and do not approach where people are speaking privately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect privacy and private discourse boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: 82d. Undertake not what you cannot Perform but be Carefull to keep your Promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not take on tasks you cannot fulfil; honour and keep your promises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prudence in committing to obligations; reliability is part of good manners.

rubrics_metrics.name: 83d. When you deliver a matter do it without Passion & with Discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: When fulfilling a mission, delivering a report, or opening a matter, do so dispassionately and discreetly, whether dealing with humble or high-positioned persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temper emotion and exercise discretion in conveying information, irrespective of the recipient's rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: 84th. When your Superiours talk to any Body hearken not neither Speak nor Laugh
rubrics_metrics.description: When your superiors speak to someone, do not speak, laugh, or listen (i.e., do not eavesdrop or intrude).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe strict silence and non-interference when those above you engage others in conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 85th. In Company of these of Higher Quality than yourself Speak not till you are ask'd a Question then Stand upright put of your Hat & Answer in few words
rubrics_metrics.description: When with persons of higher position, do not speak until questioned; then rise, uncover, and answer briefly unless invited to remain seated or keep your hat on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show deference by waiting to be addressed and responding with succinct respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: 86th. In Disputes, be not so Desirous to Overcome as not to give Liberty to each one to deliver his Opinion and Submit to the Judgment of the Major Part
rubrics_metrics.description: In disputes, especially in conversation, do not be so eager to win that you deny others the chance to voice opinions; whether right or wrong, acquiesce to the judgment of the majority, especially if they are your masters or judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote fair expression and defer to collective judgment or to those in authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: 87th. Let your bearing be such as becomes a Man Grave Settled and attentive; Contra dict not at every turn what others Say
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a moderately grave, composed, and attentive bearing so as not to make foolish interruptions; do not constantly contradict others but defer in matters of little consequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid trivial questions and continual contradiction; sustain judicious calmness and attentiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: 88th. Be not tedious in Discourse, make not many Digressions, nor repeat often the Same manner of Discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not preface at length with long apologies or ceremonious circumlocutions; enter promptly into the matter with moderate boldness and pursue to the end without hesitation; avoid prolixity, digressions, and frequent repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin succinctly, proceed steadily, and avoid verbose or repetitive speech patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: 89th. Speak not Evil of the absent for it is unjust
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not speak ill of a person who is absent; it is unjust to detract from someone's worth when they cannot defend themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve fairness and avoid besmirching reputations in absentia.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90th. Being Set at meat Scratch not neither Spit Cough or blow your Nose except there's a Necessity for it
rubrics_metrics.description: While seated at table, refrain from scratching, spitting, coughing, or blowing your nose unless necessary; if necessary, do it discreetly and quietly, turning your face aside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimise bodily noises and movements at the table; perform unavoidable actions with politeness and little disturbance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 91st. Make no Shew of taking great Delight in your Victuals, Feed not with Greediness; cut your Bread with a Knife, lean not on the Table neither find fault with what you Eat
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not eat like a glutton or display excessive pleasure in food or wine; do not break bread with your hands (unless small fresh rolls and others do so); do not rest arms unbecomingly on table or chair; answer modestly if asked your taste and do not complain about dishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice modesty and propriety at table; Washington's custom allowed guests to call for preferred wine, but general restraint and politeness are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 92d. Take no Salt or cut Bread with your Knife Greasy
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking salt be careful that the knife is not greasy; if necessary clean the knife or fork properly on a piece of bread or napkin, but never wipe it on the whole loaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid greasy utensils and improper cleaning methods that soil shared bread; use discreet, sanitary means to clean cutlery.

rubrics_metrics.name: 93d. Entertaining any one at table it is decent to present him w't meat, Undertake not to help others undesired by y'e Master
rubrics_metrics.description: When entertaining, it is proper to offer food to a guest and present dishes near them; do not help others without the master's desire or authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the host's primacy in serving and do not usurp serving roles or offer help that the host does not want.
